results.note: Reproduced at HEAD at all 8 builtins / 9 sites (test/[, shift, exit, return, read -n/-N/-t/-u, mapfile -n, umask, ulimit): underscore-separated digits are accepted via Python int(); umask and ulimit silently APPLY the wrong value. grep confirms the int() calls remain at psh/builtins/test_command.py:435, positional.py:33, core.py:51, function_support.py:1012, system_builtins.py:50 (int(mode, 8) — accepts '0_2' and '0o755'), limits.py:236, read_builtin.py:528/552/562, mapfile_builtin.py:193/204/215. Notes: (a) the original 'ulimit -c 1_0' repro is confounded on macOS because 'ulimit -c 0' also lowers the hard limit, so psh fails with 'not allowed to raise maximum limit' for a different reason; the clean discriminator is 'ulimit -S -n 2_56' which psh applies (256). (b) 'read -u 1_0' is likewise confounded (fd 10 not open -> EBADF in psh); 'read -u 0_0' cleanly shows psh reading fd 0 where bash rejects. (c) Minor oracle wording drift, NOT a behavior change: bash 5.3.15's test says '1_0: integer expected' whereas bash 5.2 (and the report's bash_expected, and psh's own rejection message for 0o10) say 'integer expression expected'; rc=2 semantics are unchanged. The '0o' prefix is correctly rejected by test/exit in psh (str->int without base doesn't accept 0o); it leaks only through umask's int(mode, 8).
